findings.description: The MySQL 8.0 parameter group sets only character set parameters and does not set require_secure_transport = ON, so the catalog database will accept unencrypted client connections, permitting cleartext transmission of credentials and data.

The RDS master username and the password variable are interpolated directly into the EC2 user_data script, which is stored unencrypted in instance metadata and readable by anything that can reach the IMDS endpoint (including SSRF from the PHP app) or anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute. The plaintext credential also lands in Terraform state and on disk in /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc.

The bootstrap installs only httpd with a plain HTTP index.php serving a form that collects employee names and addresses; no TLS listener or certificate is configured, so submitted personal data and any session data travel unencrypted.

No root_block_device or ebs_block_device block with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance's EBS volume (which holds the database credentials written to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc) may be created without encryption at rest unless account-level default EBS encryption happens to be enabled.

No metadata_options block is set, so IMDSv1 (token-optional) remains enabled. Combined with an attached instance profile and a public-facing PHP application, this materially increases the risk that an SSRF flaw yields the role's temporary credentials and the plaintext user_data containing the DB password.
storage_encrypted is explicitly set to false, so the MySQL database volume and snapshots store catalog data in cleartext at the storage layer with no KMS protection.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the RDS instance a public endpoint reachable from the internet, exposing MySQL to credential-stuffing and exploitation attempts; combined with the exported endpoint output this significantly widens attack surface.

The master password is supplied through var.password and the username is hard-coded to the default 'admin', encouraging credentials to be committed or stored in plaintext Terraform state rather than managed by Secrets Manager; ignore_changes on password also prevents rotation through Terraform.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*", violating least privilege. Because this role is attached via the instance profile to the internet-facing catalog_app_server, compromise of that host yields full control over all S3 data, EC2 infrastructure and RDS instances, including privilege-escalation paths such as modifying DB master passwords or launching instances with other roles.

Egress allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the database security group, permitting unrestricted outbound connections that facilitate data exfiltration or command-and-control if the database host is compromised.
